name: model-security-threats
job: Model security threats for a trust boundary before implementation and produce a Threat Model and Security Design Contract.

inScope: Defining subject, objectives, assets, and unacceptable outcomes
Modeling components, trust boundaries, privileges, and flows
Deriving misuse cases and ranking threats with evidence-bounded likelihood
Designing controls with verification and residual-risk ownership
outOfScope: Publishing exploit-enabling detail beyond authorized audiences

inputs: System, feature, or trust boundary under design
Source evidence for components, flows, and dependencies
outputs: Threat Model and Security Design Contract
Threat register with controls, enforcement points, and owners

tools: threat-enumeration aids (STRIDE, attack trees) as coverage aid only
data: source evidence for the real candidate and environment
permissions: protected storage and audience allowlist for the model

failureSemantics: A generic checklist is not a threat model; no taxonomy proves completeness; a control is never effective without implementation and verification evidence; the model never accepts its own material residual risk.

outcome.observable: A Threat Model and Security Design Contract linking system elements to credible threats, controls with enforcement points and owners, falsifiable verification, and owned residual risk with review triggers.
